items.title: Ubiquitous Kelvin–Helmholtz instabilities driving plasma mixing on the Sun
items.summary: High-spatial-resolution observations of the solar photosphere reveal a far more complex and dynamic solar scene than previously observed and show that ubiquitous Kelvin–Helmholtz instabilities drive plasma mixing on the Sun.

items.title: An entangling gate for dual-rail erasure qubits
items.summary: A fast, low-error entangling gate for dual-rail cavity erasure qubits preserves a strong error hierarchy, advancing scalable quantum error correction with substantially improved fault-tolerant performance.

items.title: Encapsulation epitaxy of air-stable 2D superconductors for quantum circuits
items.summary: An ‘encapsulation epitaxy’ mechanism is used to grow air-stable, two-dimensional superconducting films at the interface of a 2D–3D hybrid substrate, holding promise for use in fabrication of superconducting quantum circuitry.

items.title: Stimulation modulates gene-linked cell assemblies in the human brain
items.summary: Stimulation of human cortex reorganizes neural assemblies and induces cell-type-specific gene regulatory programs, establishing an ex vivo framework that links stimulation parameters to circuit and transcriptional responses for designing targeted neuromodulatory therapies.

items.title: A compendium of next-generation patient-derived models for diverse cancers
items.summary: The international collaboration of the Human Cancer Models Initiative presents a comprehensive resource of next-generation cancer models from 2,780 donors with 25 cancer types and integrated tumour–model genomic, transcriptomic and epigenomic analyses.

items.title: The Virtual Tissues foundation model resolves spatial proteomics across scales
items.summary: Virtual Tissues (VirTues), a foundation model for spatial proteomics that captures tissue organization across scales, supports marker reconstruction, cell segmentation and typing, niche annotation, spatial biomarker discovery and patient stratification across heterogeneous panels and datasets.

items.title: Pseudogap in a Fermi–Hubbard quantum simulator
items.summary: A cold-atom quantum simulator reveals the pseudogap metallic state in the Hubbard model, mapping its phase diagram and advancing understanding of doped Mott insulators and high-temperature superconductivity.

items.title: A tumour-derived organoid biobank maps cancer gene dependencies
items.summary: A clinically annotated multi-omic organoid resource with matched tumour samples from 256 patients across 5 cancers maps gene dependencies, reveals subtype-specific vulnerabilities and uncovers treatment-driven changes, expanding mechanistic insight and models for precision oncology.

items.title: Vacuum birefringence and the polarized X-ray emission from a radio magnetar
items.summary: Polarization measurements of the magnetar 1E 1547.0−5408 provide strong evidence that vacuum birefringence shapes X-ray propagation, offering an important observational test of quantum electrodynamics in extreme magnetic fields.

items.title: FNIP1 variants are associated with favourable metabolism in 1 million humans
items.summary: The FNIP1 pathway has a role in human energy metabolism, and its inhibition is a potential therapeutic strategy in cardiometabolic disease.

items.title: Maps of chromosomal regions crucial for cell division reveal high diversity
items.summary: Centromeres are regions of chromosomes that are required for cell division. Complete sequence characterization of centromeres from a diverse group of 65 individuals reveals dynamic and rapid patterns of mutational change, providing information about centromere evolution and function.

items.title: More muscle, less belly fat: mutations to a gene are linked to wide-ranging benefits
items.summary: Analysis of one million diverse genomes yields mutations associated with lower risk of diabetes, heart disease and other ‘cardiometabolic’ conditions.

items.title: An expanded codebook of human transcription factor DNA-binding specificity
items.summary: Results from a panel of assays that analyse different aspects of DNA sequence specificity reveal more than 100 new motifs to aid the characterization of putative human transcription factors.

items.title: ZFP36L2 orchestrates stress-adaptive plasticity in regeneration and cancer
items.summary: The RNA-binding protein ZFP36L2 mediates stress-adaptive plasticity in intestinal regeneration and colorectal cancer metastasis.

items.title: A dependency map enhanced with next-generation 3D cancer models
items.summary: Integration of genome-scale CRISPR screening data from traditional cell lines and next-generation cancer models expands the representation of tumour subtypes and genomic alterations in The Cancer Dependency Map.

items.title: Antigen presentation by CD40<sup>+</sup>MHC-II<sup>+</sup> astrocytes promotes CNS autoimmunity
items.summary: Astrocytes promote central nervous system (CNS) immunity through antigen presentation and activation of CD40 in astrocytes by CD40L expressed by CD4+ T cells in a model of experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis.

items.title: Virus reactivation in acute and long COVID-19
items.summary: Chronic reactivation of distinct herpesviruses and anelloviruses occur during acute and long COVID-19, and track with disease severity, inflammation and outcomes, revealing immune signatures with prognostic potential.

items.title: Membranolytic peptide programs immunogenic cell death for cancer therapy
items.summary: The synthetic-acid-responsive membranolytic peptide aMPC16-CA50 induces immunogenic membranolytic cell death in tumour cells, robustly potentiating immune checkpoint blockade therapy.

items.title: DCAF11-dependent molecular glue degrader activated by glutathionylation
items.summary: M12 is a metabolically activated molecular glue that recruits diverse proteins to DCAF11 for ubiquitin-mediated degradation, revealing a glutathione-dependent mechanism that broadens targeted protein degradation across multiple substrates.

items.title: A cholinergic hub in the nucleus accumbens gates opioid-reward learning
items.summary: Cell-type-specific opioid blockade in accumbal cholinergic interneurons abolishes morphine-reward learning without impairing analgesia and decouples morphine-evoked dopamine elevations from acetylcholine dips, suggesting pro-cholinergic strategies to limit early opioid reward acquisition.

items.title: An ancient mitochondrial program tunes translation to haem availability
items.summary: An evolutionarily conserved mitochondrial haem-sensing mechanism that predates the emergence of haemoglobin-based oxygen transport could have therapeutic value in iron deficiency disorders.

items.title: Can empty space interact with light — and even change its properties?
items.summary: Observations of a magnetized stellar core indicate that in an ultra-strong magnetic field, empty space can polarize light.

items.title: First poo transplant to treat food allergy in people has ‘exciting’ results
items.summary: Existing treatments for food allergy are limited.

items.title: Universal vaccine for pneumococcal disease moves closer to reality
items.summary: Targeting shared proteins could help to control bacterial subtypes that current vaccines do not protect against.

items.title: Junk plastic turns into high-value commodity with chemistry trick
items.summary: Researchers untangle the chemistry behind turning PVC into high-grade motor lubricant — plus, how engineered yeast can help make a cancer drug.

items.title: In situ particle-to-fibre transformation of hydrogels for 3D printing
items.summary: A three-dimensional printing method transforms hydrogel particles into aligned microfibres during extrusion, creating structural anisotropy to accelerate muscle tissue regeneration.

items.title: Amygdala astrocyte primary cilium mechanisms contribute to stress behaviours
items.summary: Amygdala astrocyte primary cilia are disrupted during stress, and their restoration leads to improvements in stress-related behaviour in mice.

items.title: Upcycling of polyvinyl chloride into polyalphaolefin lubricants
items.summary: A mild chemical process upcycles polyvinyl chloride waste into polyalphaolefin lubricants with tunable properties, offering an economical route to plastic recycling and improved carbon circularity.

items.title: Levitating sensor for magnetic fields could detect ultrafaint brain activity
items.summary: The device’s simple design could rival much more complex alternatives in biophysics research — and could even be used to search for dark matter.

items.title: Thermally evaporated perovskite/silicon tandems via formamidinium eutectic
items.summary: Thermally evaporated perovskite/silicon tandems via formamidinium eutectic

items.title: Uncovering the mechanism of female restitution in sugarcane hybrids
items.summary: Female restitution in interspecific sugarcane hybrids between Saccharum officinarum and Saccharum spontaneum arises from second division restitution, as haplotype-resolved F1 genomes reveal duplicated, partially recombined maternal chromatids and distinctive recombination signatures, resolving its meiotic mechanism and enabling breeding strategies to accelerate crop improvement.

items.title: Briefing Chat: Is DNA repair the secret to a long life? Whales and mole rats offer tantalizing hints
items.summary: Nature staff discuss how animal studies are starting to uncover how DNA repair could prolong life, and how COVID-19 can reawaken dormant viruses.

items.title: AI agents are checking the scientific literature — and spotting decades-old errors
items.summary: The technology is proving adept at finding faults in decades-old papers and reference databases.

items.title: Operational Tropical Cyclone Forecasting with AI
items.summary: Operational Tropical Cyclone Forecasting with AI

items.title: This AI tool claims to pick the top 1% of preprints. Should researchers trust it?
items.summary: QED Science says that its metrics reduce bias by assessing papers solely on the basis of their originality and validity.

items.title: Heatwaves have killed millions. Here’s how scientists tally lives lost
items.summary: Two very different methods are used to estimate the human toll of heatwaves such as those now hitting parts of Asia and Europe.

items.title: Why environmental treaties must also address mental health
items.summary: Global conventions have mainly overlooked the psychological and social impacts of climate change, biodiversity loss and pollution. Here’s how to change that.

items.title: How a steady drip-drip can erode the hardest stone
items.summary: Measuring the deformation of a surface hit by a falling droplet offers insights into water’s erosive power.

items.title: Exclusive: the science papers that patents cite the most
items.summary: Nature reveals the studies that are mentioned most often in patent filings — and why.

items.title: I caught my students using AI to cheat in an exam — here’s what universities must do to stamp this out
items.summary: Without strong standards and smart oversight, artificial intelligence risks eroding the foundations of higher education.

items.title: Pumas are drivers’ guardian angels
items.summary: Vehicles are less likely to smash into deer on the road where the big cats are on patrol.

items.title: Scientists up in arms about cuts to UK physics and astronomy
items.summary: Funding is being terminated for projects including a future CERN experiment and the iconic Lovell Telescope.

items.title: James Bond, not Bond James: why scientific publishing must respect name order
items.summary: Databases and submission systems are often inflexible. Can’t publishers do more on author names?

items.title: Despite global turmoil, Gen Z researchers are not giving up
items.summary: Four researchers born after 1997 describe how they stay motivated and cultivate resilience during difficult times.

items.title: What to do when you have too many PhD projects on the go
items.summary: By ruthlessly narrowing down his priorities, Zachary Sentell managed to publish several papers in the final year of his PhD and graduate on time.
